Foreman run at 09:27: all 8 FEBio runs are healthy, I fixed one CPU placement problem, and both queues are empty, so the account will go idle when these runs finish.

- **CPU is the limit now:** 30.8 of the 32-core quota is in use, and the account is being throttled for 5.5 s out of every 5 s (an hour ago it was 0.007 s). The extra load is 4 gate2 `run_one.py` reruns that the interactive session started at 09:10. Their `timeout 1800` will stop them by about 09:40 at the latest. I didn't stop them: they belong to that session and are making progress.
- **Memory:** 133.3 of 137.4 GB, but only 37.4 GB is held by programs; the rest is file cache the system can free. No out-of-memory kills.
- **GPUs:** none is free for new work. GPUs 0, 5 and 6 are full of other users' jobs, and 1–4 are shared with my runs.
- **FEBio runs:** every log was written in the last 10 s and none is hung or dead. physF4_p083 moved on to its w_flexion part around 09:18. No FEBio run finished in the last hour; the last one was physF4_p139 at 08:13.
- **Services:** every tmux service in `resume_all.sh` is up.
- **Action:** physF4dt_p061 had its 4 threads spread over CPUs on different memory nodes, and two of them kept sharing CPU 44. I re-pinned it to CPUs 75–78 on node 4, which holds most of its memory. Each thread now has its own CPU and its log is still growing. It was not restarted, so no progress was lost.
- **Not covered on restart:** the gate2 reruns are outside the task queue and `resume_all.sh`, so a server restart would lose them.

**Needs a person:**
- Queue the next decided work before the 8 FEBio runs finish.
- If gate2 is rerun again, submit it as `work/ops/tasks/queue/*.json` so it survives a restart and is scheduled alongside the FEBio load.
- Still open from earlier reports: core masks in h06/h18 should stay within one memory node.
